name: Clustering Papers by Meaning
title: Clustering Papers by Meaning
answer: Clustering papers by meaning groups research works according to what they are about rather than where they were published or who wrote them. It sits inside citation mapping and discovery, where the goal is to surface related work that keyword search and citation links alone tend to miss. A typical use is finding the neighbourhood around a paper, so a reader can see the other works that occupy the same idea space. The unit of analysis is usually the paper abstract or full text, sometimes combined with its citation context.

sections.body: Clustering papers by meaning groups research works according to what they are about rather than where they were published or who wrote them. It sits inside citation mapping and discovery, where the goal is to surface related work that keyword search and citation links alone tend to miss. sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on vector representations of text, produced by embedding models that turn a paper or a passage into a numeric vector. Those vectors are stored in an index that supports nearest neighbour search, which is what makes comparison across thousands of documents practical. This site's library of 319 research papers is small enough that clustering can be done in memory, while larger corpora need approximate search structures. Compute is ordinary: a single machine with a modest GPU handles embedding, and clustering itself is cheap once vectors exist.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The usual pipeline embeds each paper, reduces the vectors to a lower dimensional space, then applies a clustering algorithm such as k-means or a density based method. The number of clusters is either fixed in advance or inferred from the data, and the resulting groups are labelled by inspecting their most representative terms or papers. Quality is judged by whether clusters correspond to recognisable research themes and whether near duplicate papers land together. Because embeddings drift between model versions, the vectors and the clustering must be regenerated together rather than mixed.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The main provenance question is which text was embedded and which model produced the vectors, since a cluster is only reproducible if both are recorded. Copyright matters when full text rather than abstracts is used, and this site links to the original paper rather than reproducing it. Clustering can also amplify existing gaps in a corpus, so a group that looks coherent may simply reflect what was collected. Any downstream claim about a paper should be checked against the paper itself, and nothing here is legal advice.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Work in this area is moving toward embeddings that capture citation context and method rather than topic alone, so clusters reflect how a paper is used and not just what it mentions. Incremental clustering, where new papers join existing groups without a full rebuild, is becoming more common as libraries grow. Evaluation remains the weak point, since there is no single correct grouping of a research field. The practical direction is toward maps that a reader can navigate, with clusters as entry points into the underlying papers.
